subagent_reports.topic: Design leverage scout for marker-gated deploy worker self-roll

sources.label: Proposal and agreement
sources.summary: Contract requires explicit fail-closed capability marker, no deploy SIGTERM for marked workers, loud legacy fallback, no signals in read-only modes, 60-second convergence, unchanged crash accounting, and aligned specs/docs/tests.

sources.label: Current deploy worker refresh
sources.summary: Exact-path /proc cmdline enumeration currently treats every matching worker uniformly, emits ACTION_REQUIRED in read-only modes, and SIGTERMs all matches in mutating modes.

sources.label: Central worker spawn environment
sources.summary: buildTemporalWorkerProcessSpec already owns the allowlisted environment passed to worker children, providing one low-risk marker injection point.

sources.label: Self-roll monitor
sources.summary: Heartbeat-triggered drift checks already single-flight, owner-gated, readiness-gated, and hand generation stamping to the heartbeat.

sources.label: First-class roll lifecycle
sources.summary: restartChild already separates expected roll exits from crash accounting and resolves after replacement readiness.

sources.label: Linux proc_pid_environ manual
sources.summary: /proc/PID/environ exposes exec-time environment as NUL-separated entries and access is permission-gated, supporting exact marker parsing plus fail-closed unreadable handling.

sources.label: Node.js child_process documentation
sources.summary: spawn options.env defines child environment variables; this supports setting the marker at the existing centralized process-spec boundary.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Bounded scout found five leverage candidates, sorted by payoff/risk: (1) adopt_now—inject the exact marker in buildTemporalWorkerProcessSpec and pin its literal with focused tests; this uses the existing safe environment boundary and ties to AC1/C1/C3. (2) adopt_now—classify each exact-path PID once as marked or legacy before mode branching; marked gets advisory only, while missing/malformed/unreadable evidence follows the existing legacy bounce/failure path; ties to AC1-AC4/C1-C3. (3) design_around—make check/dry-run reuse the same classifier but remain signal-free, suppressing false ACTION_REQUIRED for marked workers while keeping an explicit legacy warning; ties to AC3 and avoids duplicated policy. (4) design_around—build AC5 convergence proof from the existing readiness-gated worker-roll and heartbeat generation paths, waiting on observable ready replacement plus lock-generation equality rather than a fixed sleep; ties to AC5. (5) adopt_now—reuse restartChild diagnostics/expectedRollExits assertions to prove marked deployment does not consume restartCount, instead of inventing a second accounting mechanism; ties to AC6/DONT3. No draft design artifact was available, so assessment validates leverage against proposal/agreement and current implementation, not a complete design document.

validation.notes: Core marker-gated direction matches existing architecture and has low-risk reuse points. Caution: design should explicitly define one classifier result model, exact marker ownership/value, read-only output semantics, and observable AC5 test mechanics before implementation.

tradeoffs: Reading /proc/PID/environ adds Linux-specific parsing and permission/race cases, but agreement already chooses fail-closed /proc evidence and preserves legacy fallback.
Central marker injection is simple and structural, but duplicated shell/TypeScript literals require contract tests to prevent drift.
Observable convergence testing is stronger than sleeping, but requires a live post-restart harness and bounded state observation.

alternatives_considered.option: Infer capability from deployed manifest or lock generation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Agreement C1/DONT2 forbids inference from on-disk state; running-process marker is structural proof.
Agreement DONT1 and legacy safety criteria require loud fallback for unmarked or unclassifiable workers.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a new deploy-to-worker control channel
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing owner-driven heartbeat self-roll already supplies convergence; a second control path adds complexity without contract benefit.

alternatives_considered.option: Marker-gated classification at the existing spawn and /proc boundaries
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reuses centralized spawn environment, exact-path process safety, existing self-roll, and existing crash-accounting separation.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1, 2, and 5 now; design around candidates 3 and 4. Keep implementation to one marker injection point, one fail-closed classifier, existing legacy bounce path, and observable convergence assertions.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Design one exact-path PID classifier returning marked-self-roll versus legacy, inject ADV_TEMPORAL_WORKER_SELF_ROLL=1 at buildTemporalWorkerProcessSpec, route marked workers to advisory/no-signal behavior in every mode, retain current bounce/failure only for legacy, and reuse worker-roll/heartbeat diagnostics for AC5/AC6 evidence.

subagent_reports.topic: Independent design validation: marker-gated deploy worker self-roll

sources.label: ADV agreement and design artifacts
sources.summary: Agreement requires fail-closed marker classification, exact-path safety, no signals in read-only modes, unchanged crash accounting, and live readiness plus lock-generation convergence within 60 seconds. Design selects one centralized marker, one fail-closed classifier, legacy fallback, and observable convergence.

sources.label: Advance Meta current deploy-worker laws
sources.summary: Current rq-deployWorkerBounce01 requires mutating deploys to SIGTERM exact-path workers by default, while rq-deployWorkerBounce02 forbids signaling in check/dry-run. Design therefore requires the explicitly planned spec-law revision before implementation can conform.

sources.label: Central worker process specification
sources.summary: buildTemporalWorkerProcessSpec already constructs the allowlisted child env, making marker injection centralized and structurally simple.

sources.label: Node.js child_process documentation
sources.summary: Child-process options.env supplies environment key-value pairs to the spawned process, validating marker injection at the existing process-spec boundary.

sources.label: Linux proc_pid_environ manual
sources.summary: /proc/PID/environ exposes the exec-time initial environment as NUL-separated entries and is permission-gated, supporting literal marker parsing and fail-closed unreadable handling.

sources.label: Existing exact-path deploy refresh
sources.summary: Current deploy code enumerates /proc cmdlines, matches the literal deployed worker-script argument, excludes the detector, signals only mutating-mode matches, and reports survivors as ACTION_REQUIRED.

sources.label: Worker self-roll monitor
sources.summary: The monitor is owner-gated and single-flight; after restartChild readiness it hands the manifest generation to the heartbeat rather than writing the lock directly.

sources.label: Heartbeat cadence and lock stamping
sources.summary: Default heartbeat cadence is 10 seconds; generation handed off after roll is persisted on the next heartbeat.

sources.label: Readiness-gated restart timing
sources.summary: Hard-kill deadline is 10 seconds and replacement ready timeout is 30 seconds.

sources.label: Expected-roll crash-accounting separation
sources.summary: Expected roll exits return before crash restartCount increment, supporting AC6 without a second accounting mechanism.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Marker-gated classification is correct, simple, and aligned with agreement C1-C3: marker injection uses the existing centralized env boundary; /proc provides running-process exec-time evidence; unreadable or nonliteral evidence can fail closed to the existing legacy path; exact-path candidate discovery remains unchanged; and expectedRollExits already excludes planned rolls from crash accounting. Current advance-meta rq-deployWorkerBounce01 still mandates SIGTERM for every exact-path worker, so the planned spec update is required and must land atomically with behavior/docs/tests. Blocking timing conflict: the existing maximum timing envelope has no margin for AC5's strict 60-second convergence—up to 10 seconds before drift check, 10 seconds for old-child hard-kill, 30 seconds for replacement readiness, and 10 seconds before heartbeat lock stamping totals 60 seconds before scheduler/filesystem overhead. Design says observe within 60 seconds but does not change this envelope or force an immediate post-readiness heartbeat, so it does not structurally guarantee the approved criterion.

blockers: AC5/SC3 timing is not structurally satisfied: existing bounded stages total the full 60-second limit (10s heartbeat detection + 10s hard-kill deadline + 30s readiness timeout + up to 10s next lock stamp), leaving no execution margin. Design must specify a supported mechanism with margin or obtain a contract amendment.
validation.notes: All other assessed decisions are supported. Spec-law conflict is intentional and addressed by the design's explicit advance-meta update, but revised marker-gated normative scenarios must replace the current unconditional bounce law before acceptance.

tradeoffs: Explicit process markers provide strong running-code capability evidence but depend on Linux /proc visibility; fail-closed legacy handling preserves safety at the cost of one final bounce or loud failure for unmarked/unreadable workers.
Reusing exact-path discovery and existing self-roll/crash-accounting paths minimizes new machinery, but shell and TypeScript marker literals need deterministic contract tests to prevent drift.

Immediate post-readiness lock stamping through the existing heartbeat writer can create timing margin, but adds lifecycle-to-heartbeat coordination; reducing stage timeouts is simpler mechanically but reduces shutdown/readiness tolerance; extending the 60-second contract changes approved user expectations.

alternatives_considered.option: Marker-gated classification at centralized spawn and existing exact-path /proc boundary
alternatives_considered.rationale: Structural proof, preserves legacy safety, and reuses existing architecture.

alternatives_considered.option: Infer capability from manifest, timestamp, or lock generation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Proves deployed state rather than running-code capability and violates agreement C1/DONT2.
Violates fail-closed legacy transition requirements DONT1/C3.
Preserves current spec but defeats approved objective SC1 and continues cross-session disruption.

alternatives_considered.option: Persist generation immediately after readiness via the existing heartbeat controller
alternatives_considered.rationale: Could create AC5 timing margin while retaining heartbeat as sole lock writer, but design does not currently specify this coordination and OOS2 boundary needs confirmation.

alternatives_considered.option: Reduce hard-kill/readiness budgets or amend the 60-second contract
alternatives_considered.rationale: Either changes operational tolerance or approved acceptance semantics; requires orchestrator/user decision rather than validator invention.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Do not pass design gate yet. Preserve marker/classifier architecture, but resolve AC5 explicitly: choose and document a timing mechanism with measurable slack under 60 seconds, or amend the approved bound. Then state exact revised rq-deployWorkerBounce01 marker-gated scenarios and keep spec, generated docs, implementation, and tests atomic.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Retain centralized marker injection, one fail-closed per-PID classifier, exact-path discovery, and legacy fallback. Before design approval, add an AC5 timing design with margin and explicit observable stage budgets; update advance-meta from unconditional bounce to marker-gated self-roll in the same implementation change.

subagent_reports.topic: Revalidate revised timing proof plus AC5/SC3 and advance-meta coherence

sources.label: Approved agreement AC5/SC3
sources.summary: SC3 and AC5 require post-restart deployment to produce a ready replacement and matching deployed/lock generation within 60 seconds.

sources.label: Revised design
sources.summary: Design removes the separate post-readiness periodic-heartbeat wait by requiring immediate generation stamping after replacement readiness.

sources.label: Worker heartbeat source
sources.summary: Periodic heartbeat interval is 10 seconds; controller exposes beatNow and applies handed-off bundle generation during the atomic heartbeat rewrite.

sources.label: Worker roll source
sources.summary: Current roll awaits restartChild readiness, then updates in-memory generation and hands it to the heartbeat controller; current comments still describe persistence on the next beat, which implementation must revise.

sources.label: Worker replacement source
sources.summary: Roll hard-kill deadline is 10 seconds and replacement ready timeout is 30 seconds.

sources.label: Worker replacement sequencing
sources.summary: restartChild drains or kills the old child, spawns replacement, and resolves only after replacement ready handshake.

sources.label: Plugin heartbeat wiring
sources.summary: Successful heartbeat beats fire the drift monitor without blocking heartbeat renewal.

sources.label: Advance-meta current deploy requirement
sources.summary: Current requirement mandates SIGTERM-by-default for exact-path workers; AC7/design correctly require updating it to marker-gated self-roll with fail-closed legacy fallback.

sources.label: Advance-meta singleton requirement
sources.summary: Spec makes heartbeat freshness primary lock liveness evidence and preserves safe singleton ownership/reclaim behavior.

sources.label: Node.js timers documentation
sources.summary: Node.js timer delays are thresholds rather than exact execution deadlines; exact callback timing is not guaranteed.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: PASS. Revision removes the prior blocker: worst configured nominal path is 10 seconds to drift detection + 10 seconds drain/hard-kill deadline + 30 seconds replacement readiness = 50 seconds, because generation persistence now occurs synchronously after readiness rather than waiting another 10-second heartbeat. This leaves 10 seconds nominal scheduling/atomic-write margin against AC5/SC3. Preserve the heartbeat controller as sole post-acquire lock writer: after restartChild resolves, hand off the generation and immediately await the controller's atomic beat/write path. Do not add a second direct lock writer. Current source still says 'next beat', so implementation and comments/tests must change together. Current advance-meta rq-deployWorkerBounce01 conflicts with marker-gated behavior, but design and AC7 explicitly scope its update; this is planned spec migration, not an unresolved design compromise. Node timers do not provide a hard real-time upper bound, so the 60-second statement is an operational acceptance bound validated by live proof, not a mathematical guarantee under arbitrary event-loop starvation.

validation.notes: Prior 60-second no-margin blocker resolved. No remaining contract compromise or release blocker found. Pass depends on immediate post-readiness persistence using the existing atomic heartbeat writer, exact advance-meta replacement text, deterministic boundary tests, and the required live post-restart proof.

tradeoffs: Immediate post-readiness persistence adds one synchronous lock rewrite to the roll completion path but restores 10 seconds nominal convergence margin.
Keeping heartbeat as the sole post-acquire writer avoids lost-update complexity but requires exposing/reusing its immediate atomic write path rather than writing worker.lock directly.
A 60-second live operational bound is testable, but Node timer scheduling is not a hard real-time guarantee under arbitrary event-loop starvation.

alternatives_considered.option: Immediate post-readiness write through heartbeat controller
alternatives_considered.rationale: Reuses the existing atomic sole-writer path, makes readiness and generation equality converge in the same roll completion sequence, and removes the extra periodic interval.

alternatives_considered.option: Wait for the next periodic heartbeat after readiness
alternatives_considered.rationale: Restores the prior 60-second nominal total with no scheduling margin.

alternatives_considered.option: Write worker.lock directly from worker-roll monitor
alternatives_considered.rationale: Creates a second post-acquire lock writer and weakens the existing no-lost-update invariant.

alternatives_considered.option: Continue SIGTERM bounce for explicitly marked workers
alternatives_considered.rationale: Defeats the approved objective and risks consuming lifecycle behavior the marker-gated self-roll design is intended to preserve.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Advance design gate. During planning/execution, make post-ready stamping explicitly call the heartbeat controller's immediate atomic write path after setBundleGeneration; update stale 'next beat' comments; add a boundary test proving 10s detection + 10s retirement + 30s readiness + immediate stamp; update rq-deployWorkerBounce01/02 to marker-gated semantics with fail-closed legacy fallback; then run AC5's live post-restart 60-second proof.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Proceed. Prior timing blocker is resolved. Treat immediate same-path persistence, sole-writer preservation, exact advance-meta update, and live AC5 proof as mandatory execution checks.
follow_ups: Node.js does not guarantee exact timer callback timing; document 60 seconds as a verified operational acceptance bound, not a hard real-time guarantee: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/timers.html#settimeoutcallback-delay-args
Ensure generated spec documentation changes with advance-meta, as required by AC7.
Packet supplied all identity and scope anchors; no packet-defect warning.

## Proposal

1. Confirm (post-restart, self-roll live) that a redeploy triggers owner self-roll for all current-generation workers.
2. Replace the exit-1 SIGTERM bounce with: (a) advisory note that self-roll will pick up the new manifest generation within one heartbeat, and (b) a retained loud warning ONLY when a worker is on a pre-self-roll bundle (no manifest-drift capability) and cannot self-roll.
3. Keep `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` semantics for the genuine unrollable case; drop the false-positive exit-1 for healthy self-rolling workers.
4. Update `plugin/src/deploy-local-worker-refresh.test.ts` accordingly.

### Acceptance signal
A redeploy with live self-roll workers completes exit 0 with an advisory (no false ACTION_REQUIRED); a simulated pre-self-roll worker still surfaces the loud warning.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

`scripts/deploy-local.sh` still SIGTERM-bounces deployed Temporal `worker.js` processes after sync (`refresh_deployed_temporal_workers`, ~L1115-1231) and fails the deploy run (exit 1) when workers survive the 2s grace. With `autoRollStaleWorkerBundle` now shipped, the running worker owner detects a new bundle-generation manifest and gracefully self-rolls its own child — so the cross-session SIGTERM bounce is redundant for self-rolling (post-fix) workers.

## Evidence

- Every `deploy-local.sh --fix` in this session ended with `Worker refresh: ❌ stale deployed Temporal worker(s) survived the SIGTERM grace period` (exit 1) — the bounce failing on live workers held by other sessions.
- `autoRollStaleWorkerBundle` (shipped, PR #222) makes the owner self-roll on manifest-generation drift, which is the correct, non-cross-session mechanism.

## Constraints / nuance

- The bounce may still cover transition cases the self-roll does not (e.g. a worker running a PRE-self-roll bundle that has no manifest-drift detection). Removal must not regress those.
- Must be validated against the LIVE self-roll (requires an OpenCode restart so the self-roll code is loaded), not just unit tests.

## Desired outcome

Deploy no longer emits a failing cross-session worker bounce once self-roll is the guaranteed mechanism: either remove the bounce in favor of self-roll, or downgrade it to an advisory (non-exit-1) note that self-roll will handle the roll. Preserve a clear signal when a worker genuinely cannot roll.
documents.agreement:
# Agreement

## Objectives
- Remove deploy-time cross-session SIGTERM bounce for workers that explicitly prove self-roll capability.
- Preserve safe recovery for legacy or unclassifiable workers.

## Success Criteria
- SC1: A marked current-generation worker is not signaled during a mutating deploy and deployment exits 0 with an advisory. 
- SC2: A legacy or unreadable-environment worker retains loud actionable failure semantics.
- SC3: Post-restart live deployment converges to the deployed worker generation within 60 seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: A current worker with `ADV_TEMPORAL_WORKER_SELF_ROLL=1` is left running by a mutating deploy, deployment exits 0, and output contains an advisory but no `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]`.
- AC2: A matching worker with missing, malformed, or unreadable capability evidence is treated as legacy; a SIGTERM-resistant fixture causes exit 1 and `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` with PID and recovery instruction.
- AC3: `--check` and `--dry-run` send no signals to either marked or legacy fixtures.
- AC4: Exact-path matching does not signal an unrelated Node or Bun process.
- AC5: After plugin-host restart, a deployment replacing the worker manifest yields a ready replacement and lock generation equal to the deployed generation within 60 seconds.
- AC6: The marked-worker deployment leaves crash-respawn accounting unchanged.
- AC7: Spec, generated documentation, setup guidance, archive guidance, implementation, and tests describe marker-gated self-roll with legacy fallback.

## Constraints
- C1: Capability classification fails closed; never infer self-roll support from the on-disk manifest.
- C2: Preserve existing exact-path process safety.
- C3: Maintain legacy transition behavior until a worker explicitly carries the capability marker.

## Avoidances
- DONT1: Do not remove all worker refresh protection unconditionally.
- DONT2: Do not use manifest presence or timestamps as capability proof.
- DONT3: Do not consume worker crash-respawn budget through a normal marked-worker deployment.

## Out of Scope
- OOS1: Cross-shard worker/lock discovery changes.
- OOS2: Changing in-process worker lifecycle behavior.

## Preview Applicability
- visual_surface: false
- preview_expectation: exact_route_required: false; data_state_expectation: none; viewport_expectation: none; rationale: deployment/runtime behavior only.

## Decisions
### User Decisions
- Fail closed for missing capability proof; retain SIGTERM and loud failure.
- Require live post-restart convergence proof within 60 seconds.
- Preserve exit 1 plus `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` for an unrollable legacy worker.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)
- Use an explicit versioned process capability marker and `/proc` environment inspection, because it proves running-code capability structurally.

## Deferred Questions
- None.

## Sign-Off
- User approved criteria and agreement on 2026-07-16.
documents.design:
# Design

## Architecture Overview
Deploy retains exact-path discovery and classifies each matching PID once: literal `ADV_TEMPORAL_WORKER_SELF_ROLL=1` is `self_roll`; missing, malformed, or unreadable environments are `legacy`. Marker injection remains centralized in worker process-spec construction.

## Key Decisions
- Marked workers receive advisory/no signal; legacy workers retain SIGTERM, grace, and survivor `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` failure.
- One classifier serves mutating, `--check`, and `--dry-run`; read-only modes never signal.
- Running-process marker is capability authority; manifests/timestamps cannot prove running code.
- Heartbeat remains sole lock writer. Immediately after replacement readiness, self-roll calls the heartbeat controller's generation setter and awaits its atomic write path; it does not create a second lock writer or wait for the next 10-second beat.

## Implementation Strategy
1. Inject exact marker in centralized child environment.
2. Add fail-closed shell classifier over exact-path PIDs.
3. Route marked/legacy output and signaling through classifier.
4. Update readiness-complete self-roll path to set generation and await heartbeat-owned atomic lock write; remove stale next-beat comments.
5. Extend marked/legacy/unreadable/unrelated/read-only fixture coverage, immediate-stamp timing test, and crash-accounting assertions.
6. Update advance-meta spec, generated docs, setup/archive/recovery guidance.
7. Run live post-restart proof: ready replacement plus lock-generation equality within 60 seconds.

## LBP Analysis
Explicit marker plus heartbeat-owned immediate post-readiness stamp provides structural capability proof and 10-second nominal margin: 10s detection + 10s retirement + 30s readiness, then immediate stamp. It avoids manifest inference, unconditional protection removal, and parallel lock writers.

## Affected Components
- Worker process-spec, worker-roll/readiness lifecycle, heartbeat controller, deploy script, worker-refresh/lifecycle tests, advance-meta spec, generated docs, setup/archive/recovery guidance.

## Design-Derived Criteria
- DC1: Only exact marker value is self-roll capable; all other states are legacy.
- DC2: Classifier runs once per exact-path PID and never broadens matching.
- DC3: Heartbeat remains sole atomic lock writer; readiness path awaits its write.
- DC4: Convergence timing test covers <=50s nominal staged budget and live acceptance remains <=60s.

## Design Leverage Scout
- 5 candidates; adopted centralized marker, single classifier, planned-roll accounting; designed around shared read-only output and observable convergence.

## Validator Result
- Initial validation failed: next-beat generation stamping consumed the full 60s maximum.
- Revalidation pass: heartbeat-owned immediate post-readiness write yields 50s nominal staged maximum and preserves sole-writer safety. Risk medium: Node timers are not hard real-time guarantees; live AC5 remains required.

## Risks / Mitigations
- `/proc` failure remains legacy/fail-closed.
- First rollout handles pre-marker workers once through legacy path.
- Contract tests pin marker literal, immediate heartbeat-owned stamp, exact-path safety, and timing boundary.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary

## Outcome

`deploy-local.sh` no longer kills healthy Temporal workers. Workers that structurally prove self-roll capability (literal `ADV_TEMPORAL_WORKER_SELF_ROLL=1` in the running process environment) are left alone during deploys — they detect the new bundle generation and roll themselves. Only legacy or unclassifiable workers still get the loud SIGTERM + `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` treatment.

## Value

Ends the "every deploy ends in ❌ stale workers survived SIGTERM, restart all your sessions" failure — which happened twice during this very release cycle and is a suspected contributor to in-flight workflow poisoning (backlog bl-F5_tYP9R). Deploys become non-disruptive for current workers while keeping fail-closed safety for old ones.

## Delivered

- Fail-closed per-PID capability classifier over exact-path worker processes (`/proc` environ inspection; anything unreadable = legacy)
- Marked workers: advisory, no signal, exit 0. Legacy workers: unchanged SIGTERM/grace/loud-failure semantics
- Heartbeat-owned immediate generation stamp after replacement readiness (sole lock writer preserved; 50s nominal staged budget)
- `--check`/`--dry-run` provably signal-free (reviewer added dry-run regression coverage)
- Spec, generated docs, setup/archive/recovery guidance updated

## Verification

- Reviewer: deterministic rows all pass (114 targeted tests + `pnpm run check` green)
- **Live proof (user-approved deploy):** branch deploy 02:48:58Z → worker restart 02:49:49Z → `worker.lock` `bundle_generation` matched deployed manifest generation `c929e329…` at 02:49:57Z heartbeat — ready replacement + generation convergence ≤ 8s (60s bound, AC5/SC3)
- Live legacy fallback also observed: pre-marker workers correctly classified legacy with `[ADV:ACTION_REQUIRED]` + exit 1
- Contract review matrix: 17/17 rows passing/respected/not-applicable

## Risks / follow-ups

- First rollout on any host passes pre-marker workers through the legacy path once (by design, C3)
- Node timers are not hard real-time; the 60s bound has ~10s nominal margin — live proof confirmed ≤ 8s in practice

| AC3 | acceptance_criterion | `--check` and `--dry-run` send no signals to either marked or legacy fixtures. | pass | --check and --dry-run send no signals to marked or legacy fixtures; reviewer added dry-run marked-worker no-signal regression coverage during acceptance review. |
| AC4 | acceptance_criterion | Exact-path matching does not signal an unrelated Node or Bun process. | pass | Exact-path matching does not signal unrelated Node/Bun processes (fixture tests, reviewer-verified 114 targeted pass). |
| AC5 | acceptance_criterion | After plugin-host restart, a deployment replacing the worker manifest yields a ready replacement and lock generation equal to the deployed generation within 60 seconds. | pass | LIVE PROOF 2026-07-17 (user-approved option b): deployed dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json generation c929e329887da70c… built_at 02:48:58Z; adv_temporal_worker_restart 02:49:49Z returned serviceable replacement (PID 1429384, fresh pollers); worker.lock schema v2 bundle_generation matched deployed generation at last_heartbeat 02:49:57Z — ready replacement + lock generation equality well within 60s. |
| AC6 | acceptance_criterion | The marked-worker deployment leaves crash-respawn accounting unchanged. | pass | Marked-worker deployment leaves crash-respawn accounting unchanged (lifecycle tests); live restart diagnostics show restartCount 0. |
| AC7 | acceptance_criterion | Spec, generated documentation, setup guidance, archive guidance, implementation, and tests describe marker-gated self-roll with legacy fallback. | pass | Spec (advance-meta), generated docs, setup/archive/recovery guidance, implementation, and tests all describe marker-gated self-roll with legacy fallback (task 3 checkpoint evidence + reviewer corpus verification). |
| C1 | constraint | Capability classification fails closed; never infer self-roll support from the on-disk manifest. | respected | Classifier fails closed; capability proven only by literal running-process marker, never by on-disk manifest (contract tests pin marker literal; pnpm run check green). |
| C2 | constraint | Preserve existing exact-path process safety. | respected | Exact-path process discovery preserved; AC4 tests prove no broadened matching. |
| C3 | constraint | Maintain legacy transition behavior until a worker explicitly carries the capability marker. | respected | Legacy transition behavior maintained until explicit marker — demonstrated live: pre-marker workers handled through legacy path on first rollout. |
| DONT1 | avoidance | Do not remove all worker refresh protection unconditionally. | respected | Worker refresh protection retained for legacy/unclassifiable workers; only proven self-roll workers exempted. |
| DONT2 | avoidance | Do not use manifest presence or timestamps as capability proof. | respected | Manifest presence/timestamps never used as capability proof (DC1; reviewer static review). |
| DONT3 | avoidance | Do not consume worker crash-respawn budget through a normal marked-worker deployment. | respected | Normal marked-worker deployment does not consume crash-respawn budget (planned-roll accounting tests; live restartCount 0). |
| OOS1 | out_of_scope | Cross-shard worker/lock discovery changes. | not_applicable | Cross-shard worker/lock discovery unchanged. |
| OOS2 | out_of_scope | Changing in-process worker lifecycle behavior. | not_applicable | In-process worker lifecycle behavior unchanged. |
